hypothesis: useBoardRowWindow's native 'scroll' listener (src/hooks/useBoardRowWindow.js:106) recomputes the visible window and calls setRange synchronously on every native scroll event, without a requestAnimationFrame gate. During a fast wheel flick this can fire the handler, and the resulting React re-render + reconciliation for newly-mounted rows/cells (PurchaseOrdersBoardRows -> multiple PurchaseOrderBoardRow -> ~25 PurchaseOrderBoardCell each, several wrapping Fluent UI Tooltip/Badge/Button), more than once per animation frame. Those extra synchronous passes stack within the same task and can compound into the very large blocking frames observed (maxLongFrameMs 1094-1970ms), well beyond what mounting ~14-row overscan alone should cost. L5 windowing already exists (v1.3, confirmed in code and via BL-005 note) so the fix targets the render-scheduling gap on top of it, not virtualization itself.
steps: In useBoardRowWindow.js, gate the scroll handler's update() call behind requestAnimationFrame with a pending-frame flag, so at most one range recompute + setRange happens per animation frame regardless of native scroll-event frequency.
Cancel any pending rAF on unmount/re-subscribe to avoid stale updates after scrollRef changes.

Wrap the row-window recompute (offsets/range) in measure('board:window-update', ...) from src/utils/perf.js so the next perf-scroll run attributes cost precisely (window-calc vs. row mount/reconciliation) instead of one lumped longframe.

Re-run playwright/perf-scroll.js (profile L) against Azure DEV after the change; if maxLongFrameMs still exceeds target, the next tier is L5 tuning (reduce PurchaseOrdersBoardRows overscan from 14, or split cell mount cost, e.g. defer non-essential per-cell Fluent wrappers like Tooltip until hover) rather than re-attempting L1.
functionalInvariants: Scrolling the PO board still renders the correct rows for any scroll position (no gaps/duplicates at window boundaries)
Sticky/pinned group header still stays visible while scrolling within a group
Expanding a PO row while scrolled still shows correct line details and correct spacer-row height
Locate-to-row (remarks) still works — windowing must still fully disable (all rows mounted) while a locate request is active
